Binary, unstructured point cloud container compatible with ROS PCLPointCloud2 layout. Holds header, dimensions (height, width), field descriptions, endianness, per-point and per-row strides, raw byte data, and density flag. Provides concatenation utilities and typed accessors to interpret bytes at a given point index and field offset. Ownership aliases include shared_ptr typedefs provided within and re-exposed typedefs in the namespace. Construction and destruction follow standard C++ semantics; no custom allocator or deleter is specified. Endianness must match for concatenation. Users must ensure field offsets and point_step are consistent with stored data when using at<T>.

Image container in the pcl namespace carrying a PCLHeader timestamp/frame, dimensions, pixel encoding string, endianness flag, row stride (step), and raw byte data buffer. Provides shared_ptr typedefs (Ptr/ConstPtr) and corresponding namespace aliases. Construction is default; fields should be populated by the producer. Ownership of the byte buffer is via std::vector. Endianness and step must match encoding. Header type and uindex_t, shared_ptr come from external headers and are not defined here.

A lightweight header structure for PCL objects containing a sequence number, a UNIX epoch timestamp in microseconds, and a coordinate frame identifier string. Provides shared_ptr aliases (Ptr, ConstPtr) and global streaming and equality operators. No custom constructors; uses aggregate initialization with default member values.

Struct holding a PCLHeader and a vector of float coefficients for a model (e.g., plane, line). Provides default constructor and stream output operator. Smart-pointer aliases Ptr and ConstPtr are declared via shared_ptr but the shared_ptr symbol is referenced, not defined here. Ownership and lifecycle follow standard value-semantics; no custom destructor or invariants are specified.

A polygonal mesh container in the pcl namespace holding a PCLHeader, a PCLPointCloud2 for vertex data, and a vector of pcl::Vertices for face indices. Provides static concatenate methods and +/+= operators to merge meshes, updating header stamp and offsetting face indices by the original vertex count. Ownership and memory are value-based for members; Ptr/ConstPtr aliases provide shared_ptr handle types.

pcl::Vertices is a simple POD-like structure representing a polygon’s vertex index list in a mesh. It contains a single member, vertices, of type Indices (defined elsewhere in PCL) that stores the indices of the vertices making up a face or polygon. It provides default construction and two convenience smart-pointer aliases (Ptr, ConstPtr).

Holds a header (timestamp/frame info) and a collection of point indices referring into a point cloud. Provides shared_ptr aliases (Ptr/ConstPtr) and stream output. The member types PCLHeader and Indices are defined elsewhere. Construction is default; no special destruction required.

objects.definition: enum NormType {L1, L2_SQR, L2, LINF, JM, B, SUBLINEAR, CS, DIV, PF, K, KL, HIK};
objects.description: Enumeration of supported norm/distance metrics selectable by selectNorm. Values include L1 (Manhattan), L2_SQR (squared Euclidean), L2 (Euclidean), LINF (Chebyshev), JM, B, SUBLINEAR, CS, DIV, PF, K, KL (Kullback–Leibler divergence for discrete PDFs), and HIK (histogram intersection kernel). Simple stopwatch utility in the pcl namespace. Measures elapsed time since last reset using steady_clock. getTime returns milliseconds, getTimeSeconds returns seconds. Construct normally; call reset to start timing. No ownership or external resources.

RAII scope timer derived from pcl::StopWatch. On destruction, prints the elapsed time in milliseconds to std::cerr with an optional title. Construct at scope entry to measure that scope. Printing side effect on destruction.

Helper to estimate event frequency over a sliding window of the most recent N events (default 30). Call event() per occurrence; getFrequency() returns Hz based on timestamps from an internal StopWatch. reset() clears state.

A PCL class that estimates 3D rigid poses from 6-DoF point correspondences. Provides APIs to compute candidate transformations using 1, 2, or 3 correspondences, collect PoseEstimate results, and exposes tunable Parameters. Instances own a Parameters struct.

A PCL utility class that computes Gaussian kernels and their derivatives and applies separable 1D convolutions along rows/columns of point cloud images (using float intensity or a user-provided accessor). Implementation details reside in pcl/common/impl/gaussian.hpp. Construction/destruction are default; no resource ownership is implied.

A class in namespace pcl representing a piecewise linear function. It stores control points in data_points_ and applies an affine transform factor_ * value + offset_. The constructor takes factor and offset; getDataPoints returns a modifiable reference to the underlying vector of control points; getValue evaluates the function at a given point (inline definition is expected in the included implementation header). Periodic timer class in namespace pcl that invokes a single registered callback at a fixed interval on an internal thread. functions.name: pcl_round
functions.signature: double pcl_round(double number)
functions.description: Rounds the input to the nearest integer value using half-away-from-zero semantics. For non-negative values it computes floor(x + 0.5); for negative values it computes ceil(x - 0.5). Returns the rounded value as a double.
requirements: Argument is a double representing the value to round.
Caller should be prepared for typical floating-point edge cases (e.g., NaN or infinities propagate through std::ceil/std::floor per implementation).
No special preconditions; function is pure and does not allocate.

functions.name: pcl::aligned_malloc
functions.signature: void* pcl::aligned_malloc(std::size_t size)
functions.description: Allocates a block of memory with 16-byte alignment. Uses the best available platform mechanism (malloc/posix_memalign/_mm_malloc/_aligned_malloc/memalign). Returns a valid pointer on success or null on allocation failure.
requirements: size specifies the number of bytes to allocate.
Memory returned must be released with pcl::aligned_free; do not mix with delete or standard free in user code.
Caller must check for a null return to detect allocation failure.
Behavior for size == 0 follows the underlying allocator; callers should avoid requesting zero bytes unless they can handle a possible null or non-dereferenceable pointer.

functions.name: pcl::aligned_free
functions.signature: void pcl::aligned_free(void* ptr)
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated by pcl::aligned_malloc (or a compatible 16-byte-aligned allocator used internally) using the matching platform-specific deallocation routine.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer obtained from pcl::aligned_malloc (or be null).
Do not pass pointers allocated with new/delete or with unrelated allocation routines.
After freeing, the pointer becomes invalid and must not be dereferenced.

functions.name: pcl::PointXYZRGBtoXYZI
functions.signature: inline void pcl::PointXYZRGBtoXYZI(const pcl::PointXYZRGB& in, pcl::PointXYZI& out)
functions.description: Converts a single PointXYZRGB to PointXYZI by copying XYZ coordinates and computing intensity as a luminance-weighted sum of RGB (0.299*R + 0.587*G + 0.114*B). Use when a grayscale intensity representation of colored 3D points is needed.
requirements: Input in.r, in.g, in.b are 8-bit color channels in the range [0, 255].
out is provided by caller and will be written with XYZ copied from in and intensity computed from in’s RGB.
No allocation is performed; out must be a valid reference.

requirements: Input in.r, in.g, in.b are 8-bit color channels in the range [0, 255].

requirements: Input in.r, in.g, in.b are 8-bit color channels in the range [0, 255].
Output ranges: out.h in [0,360), out.s in [0,1], out.v in [0,1].
out is provided by caller and will be written; XYZ is copied from in.

functions.name: pcl::PointXYZRGBtoXYZLAB
functions.signature:
template <typename PointT, pcl::traits::HasColor<PointT> = true>
inline void pcl::PointXYZRGBtoXYZLAB(const PointT& in, pcl::PointXYZLAB& out)
functions.description: Converts a single XYZRGB-like point to XYZLAB by copying XYZ and transforming sRGB to CIE L*a*b* (D65, 2° observer). Uses a lookup table to linearize sRGB before XYZ→LAB. Intended for any point type with r,g,b fields.
requirements: PointT must satisfy pcl::traits::HasColor<PointT> (provide r, g, b color channels).
Input in.r, in.g, in.b are sRGB 8-bit values in [0, 255].
out.x, out.y, out.z are copied from in; out.data[3] is set to 1.0 for homogeneous coordinates.
Color space assumptions: D65 white point; L*, a*, b* computed per standard formulas.

requirements: Input hue in.h is expected in degrees; typical range [0, 360).
Input in.s and in.v are expected in [0,1].
out.r, out.g, out.b are uint8 and are set to 0–255 via scaling.
out must be a valid reference; XYZ is copied from in.

functions.name: pcl::PointCloudDepthAndRGBtoXYZRGBA
functions.signature: inline void pcl::PointCloudDepthAndRGBtoXYZRGBA(const pcl::PointCloud<pcl::Intensity>& depth, const pcl::PointCloud<pcl::RGB>& image, const float& focal, pcl::PointCloud<pcl::PointXYZRGBA>& out)
functions.description: Back-projects a registered depth image (stored as Intensity values) and a corresponding RGB image into a PointCloud<PointXYZRGBA>. Depth values are interpreted as millimeters and converted to meters (z = depth*0.001). Pixel coordinates (u,v) are mapped to 3D using x = u*z/focal and y = v*z/focal. Color is taken from the RGB image at the same (u,v). Depth of zero is treated as missing and results in NaN XYZ.
requirements: depth and image must be registered and have identical width and height; indexing (u,v) must refer to corresponding pixels.
focal must be non-zero to avoid division by zero; typically positive focal length in pixel units.
Depth units: depth.at(u,v).intensity is expected in millimeters; zero indicates invalid/missing depth.
out is modified by push_back; caller should clear out beforehand if previous contents are not desired.

functions.name: pcl::fromPCLPointCloud2
functions.signature:
template <typename PointT>
void pcl::fromPCLPointCloud2(const pcl::PCLPointCloud2& msg, pcl::PointCloud<PointT>& cloud, const pcl::MsgFieldMap& field_map, const std::uint8_t* msg_data)
functions.description: Deserializes point data from an external binary buffer (msg_data) that matches msg’s layout into a pcl::PointCloud<PointT> using a precomputed field-map. Copies metadata (header, width, height, is_dense) from msg and fills cloud’s point data according to field_map. If a single contiguous mapping matches the full point size, rows are memcpy’d in bulk; otherwise each mapped field segment is copied. After copying, any fields that share a name but differ in datatype are cast into PointT.
requirements: PointT must be compatible with msg.fields (field names must correspond; datatypes may differ and will be cast with potential precision loss).
field_map must be created for the same PointT and msg.fields (e.g., via pcl::createMapping<PointT>(msg.fields, field_map)).
msg_data must point to at least msg.height * msg.row_step bytes (or msg.width * msg.height * msg.point_step if contiguous).
cloud is resized to msg.width * msg.height; the function returns early if that product is 0.
If field_map represents a full, contiguous copy, sizeof(PointT) must equal msg.point_step for the fast path to apply.
Casting occurs only for fields with matching names but different datatypes; missing fields are warned about (via logging) and not copied.

functions.name: pcl::toPCLPointCloud2

template <typename PointT>
void pcl::toPCLPointCloud2(const pcl::PointCloud<PointT>& cloud, pcl::PCLPointCloud2& msg, bool padding)
functions.description: Serializes a templated pcl::PointCloud<PointT> into a PCLPointCloud2 message. Populates msg.fields using PointT’s traits and writes point data either including struct padding (padding=true) or tightly packed without padding (padding=false). Copies metadata (header, width, height, is_dense).
requirements: If cloud.width == 0 and cloud.height == 0, the function treats the cloud as unorganized and sets msg.width = cloud.size(), msg.height = 1.
If cloud.width != 0 or cloud.height != 0, cloud.size() must equal cloud.width * cloud.height (checked via assert).
When padding == true, msg.point_step == sizeof(PointT) and msg.data.size() == sizeof(PointT) * cloud.size().
When padding == false, msg.fields[i].offsets are adjusted to be tightly packed and msg.point_step equals the sum of actual field sizes (no padding).
PointT must have a valid traits::fieldList specialization.

functions.name: pcl::estimateProjectionMatrix
functions.signature:
template <typename PointT>
double pcl::estimateProjectionMatrix(typename pcl::PointCloud<PointT>::ConstPtr cloud,
                                     Eigen::Matrix<float, 3, 4, Eigen::RowMajor>& projection_matrix,
                                     const pcl::Indices& indices = {})
functions.description: Estimate the 3x4 projection matrix P = K * (R | -R*t) from an organized point cloud acquired by a projective sensor (e.g., stereo, RGB-D). The computed matrix is returned via projection_matrix, and the function returns a residual error (higher values suggest the cloud was not captured by a projective device). Optionally, a subset of points can be specified via indices to drive the estimation.
requirements: cloud must be an organized point cloud originating from a projective device (e.g., stereo or Kinect).
cloud is passed as a shared-const pointer and must reference a valid point cloud object (non-null).
projection_matrix must be a valid writable 3x4 Eigen matrix stored RowMajor; it will be overwritten with the estimated projection matrix.
If indices is provided, each index must be within bounds of cloud->points and refer to valid measurements.
Callers should examine the returned residual error; a high residual indicates the point cloud is likely not projective and the estimate may be unreliable.

functions.name: pcl::getCameraMatrixFromProjectionMatrix
functions.signature:
void pcl::getCameraMatrixFromProjectionMatrix(const Eigen::Matrix<float, 3, 4, Eigen::RowMajor>& projection_matrix,
                                               Eigen::Matrix3f& camera_matrix)
functions.description: Compute the intrinsic camera matrix K from a given 3x4 projection matrix P. This implementation avoids RQ decomposition and uses P' * P'^T = K * K^T, where P' is the left 3x3 block of P. The resulting 3x3 intrinsic matrix is written to camera_matrix.
requirements: projection_matrix must be a valid 3x4 RowMajor Eigen matrix representing a pinhole camera projection matrix of the form P = K * (R | -R*t).
camera_matrix must be a valid writable 3x3 Eigen matrix; it will be overwritten with the computed intrinsics.
Input projection_matrix should have a non-singular left 3x3 block to allow recovery of K via P' * P'^T.

functions.name: pcl::utils::equal
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
bool pcl::utils::equal(T val1, T val2, T eps = std::numeric_limits<T>::min());
functions.description: Compares two values for approximate equality within a tolerance epsilon. Intended for numeric types: returns true when the absolute difference between val1 and val2 is strictly less than eps. Typical usage is for floating-point comparisons by supplying a small positive epsilon. Note: The default epsilon is std::numeric_limits<T>::min(), which is the smallest positive normalized value for floating-point types but the minimum representable value (often negative) for integral types; for non-floating T this default is usually inappropriate—callers should provide a positive eps explicitly.
requirements: T must support subtraction (operator-), comparison with eps using operator<, and be compatible with std::numeric_limits<T>::min().
The expression std::fabs(val1 - val2) must be valid; val1 - val2 must be convertible to a type accepted by std::fabs (typically arithmetic).
eps should be non-negative; for meaningful floating-point comparisons, provide a small positive eps appropriate to the scale of the values.
If T is an integral type, callers should provide a positive eps explicitly; the default std::numeric_limits<T>::min() will likely make the comparison always false or nonsensical.
Inputs should be finite numeric values for meaningful results; NaN propagation will cause the comparison to return false.

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary string buffer
# Used by fuzzer stubs for:
# - Field names in PCLPointCloud2 (should sometimes match common PCL field names)
# - Filenames/paths for filename helpers (with/without slashes and extensions)
# - General strings (frame_id, titles) with reasonable lengths
# - Raw float vectors encoded as bytes for norm functions (size multiple of 4 helpful)
#
# Strategy:
# Generate a seeded mixture of:
# 1) Common PCL field names and realistic point field schema snippets
# 2) File paths with and without directories and extensions (including multiple dots)
# 3) Random UTF-8-like and binary data including NULs
# 4) Byte sequences whose length is a multiple of 4 to decode as float arrays
# 5) Short strings for titles/frame_ids
# The result size capped <= 4096 bytes.

COMMON_FIELD_NAMES = [
    b"x", b"y", b"z", b"rgb", b"rgba", b"intensity", b"normal_x", b"normal_y", b"normal_z",
    b"curvature", b"label", b"h", b"s", b"v", b"a", b"b", b"u", b"v_tex"
]

COMMON_EXTS = [b"pcd", b"bin", b"ply", b"txt", b"dat", b"json", b"csv", b"gz"]

DIR_PARTS = [b"/", b"./", b"../", b"/tmp/", b"/var/log/", b"C:/", b"D:/data/"]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _random_float_bytes(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    # Create count floats with finite values in a reasonable range
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(count):
        # Mix of small, medium, and special values
        choice = rng.randrange(6)
        if choice == 0:
            f = 0.0
        elif choice == 1:
            f = 1.0
        elif choice == 2:
            f = -1.0
        elif choice == 3:
            f = rng.uniform(-1000.0, 1000.0)
        elif choice == 4:
            f = rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0)
        else:
            # create histogram-like non-negative
            f = abs(rng.gauss(0.0, 1.0))
        out += struct.pack('<f', f)
    return bytes(out)


def _random_field_name(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(COMMON_FIELD_NAMES)
    # random alnum
    length = rng.randint(1, 12)
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_"
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))


def _random_filename(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(rng.choice(DIR_PARTS))
    # base name possibly with dots
    base_len = rng.randint(1, 16)
    base_chars = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-"
    base = bytes(rng.choice(base_chars) for _ in range(base_len))
    # maybe multi-dot name
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base += b"." + bytes(rng.choice(base_chars) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
    # extension or none
    if rng.random() < 0.85:
        ext = rng.choice(COMMON_EXTS)
        name = base + b"." + ext
    else:
        name = base
    parts.append(name)
    return b"".join(parts)


def _schema_snippet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a small pseudo PCL fields schema like: "x y z rgb intensity"
    k = rng.randint(3, 7)
    fields = [ _random_field_name(rng) for _ in range(k) ]
    return b" ".join(fields)


def _random_frame_id(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Typical frame ids like "map", "odom", "base_link", or random short strings
    common = [b"map", b"odom", b"base_link", b"camera_link", b"world"]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(common)
    # allow slashes sometimes
    tokens = [b"base", b"laser", b"imu", b"cam", b"lidar", b"link", b"optical"]
    t = rng.choice(tokens) + b"_" + rng.choice(tokens)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        t = b"/" + t
    return t[:64]


def _binary_block_with_nuls(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Include some NULs and mixed bytes
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    data = bytearray(_rand_bytes(rng, n))
    # sprinkle NULs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, max(1, n // 8))):
        idx = rng.randrange(n) if n > 0 else 0
        if n > 0:
            data[idx] = 0
    return bytes(data)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a recipe to target different stub needs
    recipe = rng.randrange(6)

    if recipe == 0:
        # File path oriented buffer with extra random tail
        buf = bytearray()
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
            part = _random_filename(rng)
            buf += part + b"\n"
        # Append a schema line
        buf += _schema_snippet(rng) + b"\n"
        # Cap size
        return bytes(buf[:4096])

    if recipe == 1:
        # Field names repeated to increase chance getFieldIndex picks an existing one
        k = rng.randint(5, 40)
        items: List[bytes] = []
        for _ in range(k):
            items.append(_random_field_name(rng))
        # newline and space separated
        sep = b"\n" if rng.random() < 0.5 else b" "
        data = sep.join(items)
        return data[:4096]

    if recipe == 2:
        # Float vector bytes (length multiple of 4), possibly two concatenated vectors
        count1 = rng.randint(0, 256)
        count2 = rng.randint(0, 256)
        a = _random_float_bytes(rng, count1)
        b = _random_float_bytes(rng, count2)
        # Optional delimiter
        delim = b"" if rng.random() < 0.7 else b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"
        data = a + delim + b
        return data[:4096]

    if recipe == 3:
        # Mixed content: frame_id, filenames, schema, and binary block with NULs
        parts = []
        parts.append(_random_frame_id(rng) + b"\n")
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            parts.append(_random_filename(rng) + b"\n")
        parts.append(_schema_snippet(rng) + b"\n")
        parts.append(_binary_block_with_nuls(rng, 512))
        data = b"".join(parts)
        return data[:4096]

    if recipe == 4:
        # Plain random ASCII-ish string with possible slashes and dots to exercise filename helpers
        alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789._-/\\ "
        n = rng.randint(1, 1024)
        data = bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
        return data

    # recipe == 5
    # Structured block: first a count and that many field names, then two float arrays
    buf = bytearray()
    cnt = rng.randint(3, 20)
    for i in range(cnt):
        nm = _random_field_name(rng)
        buf += nm
        buf += b"\n" if i % 2 == 0 else b" "
    buf += b"\n"
    buf += _random_float_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 200))
    buf += _random_float_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 200))
    return bytes(buf[:4096])

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces an arbitrary binary blob tailored to exercise the
# provided fuzzing stubs. The stubs consume bytes as sequences of floats/ints
# (via memcpy) and as string data for filling PCLPointCloud2::data.
#
# Strategy:
# - Create a buffer composed of several regions to serve different consumers:
#   1) A header region containing multiple 4-byte float/int patterns to ensure
#      at least 32+ bytes are available for vector/angle stubs.
#   2) A palette of repeated patterns (NaN, Inf, zero, small/large magnitudes,
#      negatives, normals) but sanitized to finite values where a stub explicitly
#      sanitizes non-finite values, while still including edge-like values such
#      as -0.0 and denormals.
#   3) A larger payload of varied bytes for filling msg.data in fromPCLPointCloud2
#      and to supply sufficient floats for norms/median/mean stubs.
# - Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded randomness to vary widths/heights/paddedness-triggering bytes in stubs
#   (they sample from this blob via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)).
#
# Note: We include some canonical float encodings (little-endian) and repeated
# blocks to guarantee enough data regardless of where the stubs slice the blob.


def _pack_floats(vals: List[float]) -> bytes:
    return b"".join(struct.pack('<f', v) for v in vals)


def _pack_ints(vals: List[int]) -> bytes:
    return b"".join(struct.pack('<i', v) for v in vals)


def _rand_floats(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> List[float]:
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        # Mix of ranges to trigger different code paths; keep finite
        choice = rng.randint(0, 5)
        if choice == 0:
            out.append(rng.uniform(-1e-6, 1e-6))
        elif choice == 1:
            out.append(rng.uniform(-10.0, 10.0))
        elif choice == 2:
            out.append(rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6))
        elif choice == 3:
            # edge-ish values but finite
            out.append(0.0 if rng.random() < 0.5 else -0.0)
        elif choice == 4:
            out.append(1.0 if rng.random() < 0.5 else -1.0)
        else:
            out.append(rng.gauss(0.0, 5.0))
    return out


def _rand_ints(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> List[int]:
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        # Mix signed ranges; stubs often use unsigned modulo
        choice = rng.randint(0, 3)
        if choice == 0:
            out.append(rng.randint(-2**31 + 1, 2**31 - 1))
        elif choice == 1:
            out.append(rng.randint(-1000, 1000))
        elif choice == 2:
            out.append(0)
        else:
            out.append(rng.randint(1, 2**16))
    return out


def _canonical_float_patterns() -> bytes:
    # Finite canonical values commonly useful for geometry/stats
    vals = [
        0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 0.5, -0.5, 2.0, -2.0,
        1e-6, -1e-6, 1e6, -1e6, 3.1415927, -3.1415927,
        90.0, -90.0, 180.0, -180.0,
    ]
    return _pack_floats(vals)


def _xyz_block(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct interleaved XYZ float triplets to be meaningful for clouds
    bs = bytearray()
    for _ in range(count):
        x, y, z = rng.uniform(-10, 10), rng.uniform(-10, 10), rng.uniform(-10, 10)
        bs += struct.pack('<fff', x, y, z)
        # If a padded layout is chosen (point_step 16), the consumer ignores 4B pad
        pad = struct.pack('<f', rng.uniform(-100, 100))
        bs += pad
    return bytes(bs)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Header region with at least 32 bytes for getAngle3D (8 floats = 32B)
    # Two 4-float vectors for v1 and v2
    v1 = [rng.uniform(-5, 5), rng.uniform(-5, 5), rng.uniform(-5, 5), rng.uniform(-5, 5)]
    v2 = [rng.uniform(-5, 5), rng.uniform(-5, 5), rng.uniform(-5, 5), rng.uniform(-5, 5)]
    parts.append(_pack_floats(v1 + v2))

    # 2) Canonical finite float palette
    parts.append(_canonical_float_patterns())

    # 3) Some random floats for stats/median/norms
    parts.append(_pack_floats(_rand_floats(rng, 64)))

    # 4) Some random ints for median and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) use
    parts.append(_pack_ints(_rand_ints(rng, 32)))

    # 5) Construct a larger payload that can fill PCLPointCloud2::data
    # Create a small randomized organized cloud payload: choose dimensions that
    # the stub will compute from bytes via modulo. We just provide enough data.
    # Compose several XYZ(padded) blocks to ensure enough contiguous bytes.
    xyz_blocks = []
    # Between 2 and 6 rows of 16 points each (to supply sizable row_step*height)
    rows = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(rows):
        xyz_blocks.append(_xyz_block(rng, 16))
    parts.append(b"".join(xyz_blocks))

    # 6) Additional random bytes to diversify FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumption
    tail_len = rng.randint(128, 512)
    parts.append(rng.randbytes(tail_len) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else os.urandom(tail_len))

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    # Trim to 4096 bytes if necessary
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not blob:
        blob = b"\x00\x00\x80?"  # 1.0f

    return blob

import os

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-"
    return b"".join(bytes([alphabet[rng.randrange(len(alphabet))]]) for _ in range(n))

def _pcd_header_ascii(rng: random.Random, width: int, height: int, fields: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Build a minimal valid ASCII PCD header followed by no data (consumer won't parse here, but valid anyway)
    sizes = [4 for _ in fields]
    types = ['F' for _ in fields]
    counts = [1 for _ in fields]
    header = []
    header.append("# .PCD v0.7 - Point Cloud Data")
    header.append("VERSION 0.7")
    header.append("FIELDS " + " ".join(fields))
    header.append("SIZE " + " ".join(str(s) for s in sizes))
    header.append("TYPE " + " ".join(types))
    header.append("COUNT " + " ".join(str(c) for c in counts))
    header.append(f"WIDTH {width}")
    header.append(f"HEIGHT {height}")
    header.append("VIEWPOINT 0 0 0 1 0 0 0")
    header.append("POINTS " + str(width*height))
    header.append("DATA ascii")
    txt = "\n".join(header) + "\n"
    # Optionally add a few ASCII points
    num_pts = min(width*height, rng.randint(0, 5))
    for _ in range(num_pts):
        vals = [f"{rng.uniform(-10.0, 10.0):.6f}" for _ in fields]
        txt += " ".join(vals) + "\n"
    return txt.encode('ascii')

def _pcd_header_binary(rng: random.Random, width: int, height: int, fields: List[str]) -> bytes:
    sizes = [4 for _ in fields]
    types = ['F' for _ in fields]
    counts = [1 for _ in fields]
    header = []
    header.append("# .PCD v0.7 - Point Cloud Data")
    header.append("VERSION 0.7")

    header.append("SIZE " + " ".join(str(s) for s in sizes))

    header.append("COUNT " + " ".join(str(c) for c in counts))
    header.append(f"WIDTH {width}")
    header.append(f"HEIGHT {height}")
    header.append("VIEWPOINT 0 0 0 1 0 0 0")
    header.append("POINTS " + str(width*height))
    header.append("DATA binary")
    txt = "\n".join(header) + "\n"
    # Add a small binary blob matching point_step = 4*len(fields)
    point_step = 4 * len(fields)
    n_points = min(width*height, rng.randint(0, 8))
    blob = bytearray()

def _make_random_text_file(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Random text content to exercise reading directory entries that might be opened/peeked
    parts = []
    # Optional shebang or comment
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(b"# comment\n")
    # Random lines
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10)):
        line = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 40)
        parts.append(line + b"\n")
    return b"".join(parts)

def _compose_directory_seed(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose a multi-file payload intended to be written into several files by the harness.
    # We return one buffer; the harness creates additional .pcd/.txt files on its own.
    # Our buffer can resemble a plausible .pcd file to influence any content-based logic.
    choice = rng.random()
    width = rng.randint(1, 8)
    height = rng.randint(1, 4)
    field_sets = [["x","y","z"], ["x","y","z","intensity"], ["x","y","z","rgb"]]
    fields = field_sets[rng.randrange(len(field_sets))]
    if choice < 0.4:
        return _pcd_header_ascii(rng, width, height, fields)
    elif choice < 0.8:
        return _pcd_header_binary(rng, width, height, fields)
    else:
        # Generic text plus some .pcd-like markers to trick simple scanners
        txt = _make_random_text_file(rng)
        trailer = b"\n# .PCD v0.7\nFIELDS x y z\n"
        return (txt + trailer)[:4096]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    data = _compose_directory_seed(rng)
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
